en.headline: Palace Museum opens Qing imperial workshops exhibition
en.dek: Design for the Forbidden City, a joint show with the Palace Museum in Beijing, puts 157 objects on view from Wednesday, including 14 Grade-One relics.
body: The Hong Kong Palace Museum opened a new special exhibition on Wednesday examining the Qing court workshops known as the Zaobanchu, jointly organised with the Palace Museum in Beijing.

The show, titled Design for the Forbidden City: Imperial Workshops of the Qing Court, displays 157 objects from the Beijing collection, including 14 nationally designated Grade-One relics. Organisers said some pieces will be rotated. Admission is included with a standard museum ticket.

Three galleries cover what the workshops were, how objects were made, and how court design treated branding, revival styles and display. Highlights named by the museum include a workshop waist badge, an antler chair associated with the Kangxi emperor, a mechanical lotus basin, and a screen whose carved cover has been described as a Qianlong-era emblem.

Museum director Wu Zhihua said the exhibition uses a contemporary design lens and multimedia to present the workshops’ organisation, materials and methods. Hong Kong designers contributed to the exhibition design. The museum is at 8 Museum Drive, West Kowloon. Ordinary hours are 10am to 6pm, extending to 8pm on Fridays, Saturdays and public holidays; it is closed on Tuesdays except public holidays.

zh.headline: 香港故宮開展「清宮製造與當代設計」
zh.dek: 與北京故宮博物院合辦的專題展星期三起開放，展出157件文物，包括14件國家一級文物。
body: 香港故宮文化博物館星期三起開放與北京故宮博物院合辦的專題展覽「清宮製造與當代設計」，以當代設計視角介紹清代造辦處。
展覽展出故宮博物院157件藏品，包括14件國家一級文物，部分展品會定期更換。觀眾憑標準門票即可入場。
三個單元分別講述何謂造辦處、器物製作與工藝創新，以及創意設計與陳設。館方點名展品包括造辦處腰牌、與康熙帝相關的鹿角椅、機械荷花盆景，以及被形容帶有乾隆標記意味的插屏。
館長吳志華表示，展覽以當代視角及多媒體呈現造辦處的沿革、物料及工序，並邀請香港設計師參與展場設計。博物館位於西九文化區博物館道8號，一般開放時間為上午10時至下午6時，周五、六及公眾假期延至晚上8時，逢周二休館（公眾假期除外）。
